title: Naming of Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Mrs Lee Suet Fern when Being Investigated for Giving False Evidence in Judicial Proceedings while Keppel Offshore & Marine Senior Staff were Not Named
what_it_is: Naming of Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Mrs Lee Suet Fern when Being Investigated for Giving False Evidence in Judicial Proceedings while Keppel Offshore & Marine Senior Staff were Not Named

sections.label: Naming in investigations questioned
sections.summary: Asked why Lee Hsien Yang and Lim Suet Fern were named while six Keppel staff were not.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs why Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Ms Lim Suet Fern are named and disclosed while being investigated for giving false evidence in judicial proceedings when the names of the six former management staff of Keppel Offshore & Marine Limited were not publicly disclosed while they were being investigated.

sections.label: Agencies do not disclose names
sections.summary: Law enforcement agencies generally do not disclose names of investigated individuals, except when offenders abscond.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The general approach is that law enforcement agencies do not disclose the names of individuals who have been, or are being investigated.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: One example when names have been disclosed is where the offender has absconded or left the jurisdiction while investigations are ongoing.

sections.label: Publicly known facts exception
sections.summary: Names may be disclosed when alleged offences and individuals are already publicly known, such as from Court findings.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: A second example would be where the facts which constitute the alleged offences and the individuals who may have committed the alleged offences, are already publicly known – for example, as a result of findings made by our Courts, and there is some public interest in disclosing that investigations are underway.

sections.label: Lee circumstances straddle examples
sections.summary: The circumstances of Lee Hsien Yang and Lee Suet Fern straddle the first two examples mentioned.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The circumstances relating to Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Mrs Lee Suet Fern straddle the first two examples that I have mentioned.

sections.label: Investigations based on findings
sections.summary: Police investigations commenced based on findings of the DT and the Court of Three Judges.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Police investigations were commenced, based on the findings of the DT and the Court of Three Judges.

sections.label: Lee couple absconded jurisdiction
sections.summary: Lee Hsien Yang and Lee Suet Fern have, in addition, absconded from jurisdiction.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Except that in the case of Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Mrs Lee Suet Fern, they have, in addition, absconded from jurisdiction.

sections.label: DT and Court finding
sections.summary: The DT and the Court of Three Judges said Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Mrs Lee Suet Fern were lying.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: To summarise, the DT and the Court of Three Judges had said Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Mrs Lee Suet Fern were lying.

sections.label: Names not disclosed policy
sections.summary: The general position is that names are not disclosed, so no cloud hangs over a person later cleared.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If the investigations show that the person is innocent or an assessment is made that his guilt cannot be established in Court, and if his name had been publicised earlier, a cloud would have hung over him until he was cleared.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Thus, the general position is that names are not disclosed.

sections.label: Weighing disclosure prejudice
sections.summary: Prejudice from disclosing the investigation for lying is marginal and weighed against public interest in Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The prejudice to him in disclosing that he was under investigations for that finding of lying, is marginal if any and has to be weighed against the public interest at stake, in disclosing the facts when the matter is being discussed in Parliament.

sections.label: CPIB investigation and AGC assessment
sections.summary: CPIB investigated thoroughly with AGC and concluded no charges could be sustained in Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The CPIB had conducted as thorough an investigation as it could with the information and powers that it possessed.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It turned all the stones it could – and assessed the evidence together with the Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC).

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: They concluded that they could not sustain any charges in Court: the conduct had taken place overseas, key witnesses are not available, key documents are not available.

sections.label: Non-disclosure policy applies
sections.summary: In these circumstances, the general policy of not disclosing investigated individuals' names applies.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In these circumstances, the general policy of not disclosing the names of individuals who have been under investigation, applies.

sections.label: Police interview and abscondees
sections.summary: They agreed to an interview, left the jurisdiction, and will not cooperate, so they are essentially abscondees from justice.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And on his first question, did the Police issue a written order – they were given an email, they promised that they will come and agreed to give an interview.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: They then left the jurisdiction and they have said both to the Police and in public that they will not cooperate with the Police.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: They will not even come back into the jurisdiction.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: That is why I said they are essentially abscondees from justice.

sections.label: Court view on lies
sections.summary: The investigation relates to the point the Courts viewed on whether they lied or did not lie, so prejudice is marginal.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The investigation relates back to that very point on which the Courts have taken a view as to whether they lied or did not lie.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: That is why I said the prejudice is very marginal, if any.

sections.label: Prejudice and public interest disclosure
sections.summary: Calculations of prejudice are made before releasing information, bearing in mind public interest may require disclosure despite some prejudice.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: You make these calculations before – what is the extent of prejudice?

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And you release the information, but always bearing in mind, sometimes public interest may require disclosure, even if it means some degree of prejudice.

sections.label: No specific CPC order
sections.summary: A specific order under the CPC was not issued.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: A specific order under the CPC was not issued.

sections.label: Reading judgments on lies
sections.summary: On what the lies were, the Member is invited to read the Disciplinary Tribunal's and Court of Three Judges' judgments.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: On the first point as to exactly what the lies were, I would invite the Member to read the Disciplinary Tribunal's judgment and the Court of Three Judges' judgment.

sections.label: Bloomberg interview timing recollection
sections.summary: The speaker will answer the question and recalls the Bloomberg interview came after Senior Minister Teo's answer.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: You do not have to withdraw the question; I will answer the question.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I am trying to now recall, but my recollection is that the Bloomberg interview came after the answer given by Senior Minister Teo.

sections.label: Prepared to debate challenges
sections.summary: If anyone challenges us on that, the speaker is prepared to debate.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If anyone challenges us on that, I am prepared to debate.
